message.content:
Let the wall temperature excess be

\[
\theta_w(x)=T_w(x)-T_\infty=\frac{A}{x},
\]

where \(A\) has units of \(\text{K}\,\text{m}\). For laminar natural convection on a vertical plate with constant ambient temperature, the local Grashof number is

\[
Gr_x=\frac{g\beta \theta_w x^3}{\nu^2}
      =\frac{g\beta A x^2}{\nu^2}.
\]

From boundary-layer similarity/scaling:

\[
\delta(x) \sim x\,Gr_x^{-1/4}
            \sim \nu^{1/2}(g\beta A)^{-1/4}x^{1/2},
\]

\[
u_{\max}(x) \sim (g\beta \theta_w x)^{1/2}
             \sim (g\beta A)^{1/2},
\]

\[
q''(x) \sim k\,\frac{\theta_w}{\delta}
          \sim k\,A^{5/4}(g\beta)^{1/4}\nu^{-1/2}x^{-3/2},
\]

\[
v_\infty(x) \sim u_{\max}\frac{\delta}{x}
             \sim \nu^{1/2}(g\beta A)^{1/4}x^{-1/2}.
\]

The total heat rate per unit spanwise width up to a distance \(x\) is

\[
Q(x)=\int q''(x)\,dx.
\]

If the \(1/x\) wall-temperature law begins at a finite distance \(x_0>0\), then

\[
Q(x)\sim 2C_q\,k\,A^{5/4}(g\beta)^{1/4}\nu^{-1/2}
       \left(x_0^{-1/2}-x^{-1/2}\right),
\]

so \(Q(x)\) approaches a finite value as \(x\to\infty\). The asymptotic \(x\)-dependent correction is proportional to \(x^{-1/2}\). If the law is extended all the way to \(x=0\), the integral diverges.

Thus the power-law variations are:

\[
q'' \propto x^{-3/2},
\]

\[
Q \propto x^{-1/2}\quad\text{as an asymptotic correction, or bounded if the lower limit is finite},
\]

\[
\delta \propto x^{1/2},
\]

\[
u_{\max} \propto x^0,
\]

\[
v_\infty \propto x^{-1/2}.
\]

Here \(v_\infty\) is the similarity scale of the normal velocity at the outer edge of the boundary layer; the literal velocity far from the surface, as \(y\to\infty\), is zero.

This circumstance is not physically obtainable if the wall temperature is literally \(A/x\) for all \(x>0\) with the leading edge at \(x=0\), because the wall temperature and the integrated heat rate are singular there. It can arise physically if the inverse-distance temperature distribution is an asymptotic behavior beginning at a finite distance \(x_0>0\) from a finite leading edge, for example a vertical plate with a localized finite heat source near the leading edge whose surface temperature decays approximately as \(1/x\) away from the source. The flow would then occur under laminar natural-convection conditions: a vertical plate, quiescent constant ambient, Boussinesq approximation, constant properties, and a range short enough that the boundary layer remains laminar.

```
“‘“local heat flux ∝ x^{-3/2}; Q is bounded, δ ∝ x^{1/2}, u_max is constant, and v∞ ∝ x^{-1/2}.”’”
```
